query: How do you change how you feel, on purpose?
why_in_two_sentences: The Conversation offers one research-grounded mechanism (two-step reappraisal) and PositivePsychology offers a genuinely comprehensive regulation toolkit with six mechanisms, micro-skills, and a strategy-selection guide. Ours is simpler and more lived (three levers moved together, why a better thought fades in minutes, state vs default with honest timelines), which answers the on-purpose phrasing more directly, but PositivePsychology's selection guide is a real structural idea we lack.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Explains why moving one lever alone fails: the feeling is produced by body, attention, and language together, so a better thought overwrites in minutes
Separates changing a state (under a minute) from changing a default (months), a timeline neither competitor gives
Explains why a built good state fades by lunchtime and why retreat shifts wear off
Addresses the toxic-positivity and posture-pseudoscience objections head-on in the FAQs
34 verbatim FAQs including whether deliberate state change is manipulative and whether it must be run forever

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer names the three levers and the under-a-minute versus months distinction, then recognition sentences; the reader gets both mechanism and honest timescale.
above_the_fold.theirs: PositivePsychology opens with key insights and a find-the-right-resource menu under a PhD byline with a PhD scientific reviewer; comprehensive, but aimed at practitioners as much as sufferers.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: What is reappraisal, and does reinterpreting the situation actually change the feeling?
Which regulation strategy fits this intensity of emotion right now?
trust_signals: The Conversation carries academic authors writing on their own studies; PositivePsychology shows a PhD author and a named PhD scientific reviewer; ours names no one and cites nothing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add a short match-the-move-to-the-moment selection note (what to do at low versus high intensity); PositivePsychology's selection guide is the one structural idea on page one that our three-lever frame does not cover.
